title: Data model
summary: Choose entities, keys, and access paths before choosing a database product.

parts.rule: Start from the operations the system must serve. Name entities, stable identifiers, relationships, cardinalities, and the keys used by high-volume reads and writes. A primary key locates the authoritative record; secondary indexes or derived tables support additional access paths at a write and storage cost. Choose a database category after this model is concrete.
parts.why: A flexible schema does not rescue a design that scans millions of records for its main read. Conversely, indexing every field makes each write maintain structures that may never be used. Connecting each query to a key exposes missing ownership, awkward many-to-many relationships, and partition hot spots before they become infrastructure problems.
parts.example: A URL shortener needs: redirect by code, create for owner, list an owner’s newest links, and disable a link. Model Link(code, destination_url, owner_id, created_at, disabled_at). Make the 7-character code the primary key because GET /a1b2c3d must locate one row directly. The owner dashboard runs WHERE owner_id=42 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20, so add a composite index on (owner_id, created_at DESC) or maintain an owner_links table with that key order. The create path writes the Link row and updates that secondary structure; the faster owner read is not free. At 10 creates per second, a year adds about 315 million rows, so estimate row and index size rather than calling the table small. A base62 code space has 62^7 possibilities—about 3.5 trillion—but random generation still needs a uniqueness constraint and retry because collisions are possible. disabled_at supports reversible or auditable disable behavior while the redirect query checks that it is null. If preview images are 5 MB each, store the bytes in object storage and keep an object key in Link metadata. This model supports the named queries before any vendor is selected; transaction needs and scale can now guide the storage choice.
parts.use: Model immediately after defining APIs and before drawing storage products. Write the top reads and writes beside the entities, including filter and sort order. Estimate cardinality and payload size, identify one authoritative writer, and explain the write cost of every extra index or denormalized view.
parts.refuse: Do not choose a database brand before keys and queries exist. Avoid a model whose hottest path requires a full scan, speculative indexes on every column, or large blobs in frequently read rows. Surrogate identifiers are not enough if the application still lacks an efficient key for its real access pattern.

body:
Rule. Start from the operations the system must serve. Name entities, stable identifiers, relationships, cardinalities, and the keys used by high-volume reads and writes. A primary key locates the authoritative record; secondary indexes or derived tables support additional access paths at a write and storage cost. Choose a database category after this model is concrete.

Why it matters. A flexible schema does not rescue a design that scans millions of records for its main read. Conversely, indexing every field makes each write maintain structures that may never be used. Connecting each query to a key exposes missing ownership, awkward many-to-many relationships, and partition hot spots before they become infrastructure problems.

Worked example. A URL shortener needs: redirect by code, create for owner, list an owner’s newest links, and disable a link. Model Link(code, destination_url, owner_id, created_at, disabled_at). Make the 7-character code the primary key because GET /a1b2c3d must locate one row directly. The owner dashboard runs WHERE owner_id=42 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20, so add a composite index on (owner_id, created_at DESC) or maintain an owner_links table with that key order. The create path writes the Link row and updates that secondary structure; the faster owner read is not free. At 10 creates per second, a year adds about 315 million rows, so estimate row and index size rather than calling the table small. A base62 code space has 62^7 possibilities—about 3.5 trillion—but random generation still needs a uniqueness constraint and retry because collisions are possible. disabled_at supports reversible or auditable disable behavior while the redirect query checks that it is null. If preview images are 5 MB each, store the bytes in object storage and keep an object key in Link metadata. This model supports the named queries before any vendor is selected; transaction needs and scale can now guide the storage choice.

[[diagram:entities]]

When to use. Model immediately after defining APIs and before drawing storage products. Write the top reads and writes beside the entities, including filter and sort order. Estimate cardinality and payload size, identify one authoritative writer, and explain the write cost of every extra index or denormalized view.

When to refuse. Do not choose a database brand before keys and queries exist. Avoid a model whose hottest path requires a full scan, speculative indexes on every column, or large blobs in frequently read rows. Surrogate identifiers are not enough if the application still lacks an efficient key for its real access pattern.
